tenures.bio:
Angel is a mysterious character, he appeared from practically nowhere in the GIWF in September 1999.  Angel then resided from Rio de Janeiro and was a patron of Tae Kwon Do.  From there he fought with his arch-nemesis Exorcizandis unfortunately twice did Angel receive defeat at the hands of Exorcizandis.  After a brief time away from the GIWF, Angel returned in the summer of 2000 but suffered a major knee injury after falling out of the ring in the 20-man over the top rumble.

From there, little is known of his whereabouts and at one time was reported to be in fact dead.  But he has returned to the UWF with his mentor and wife Ayami. In the UWF Angel hopes to take down the evil that is being inflicted on the federation and hopes to spread his word of good across the world.  

Angel himself is still wrestling in his mind with unknown dreams of ancient lands he does not remember.  It seems Angel is a little more than a mere preacher; someone doesnt want Angel to fail and will do anything to make sure he succeeds.  Who this person is, is unknown. Only time will tell.

tenures.bio:
Brody is the middle child of the O'Hara wrestling trio and the one to compete in singles wrestling, unlike his tag teaming brothers. He's got a good strong build. He has black hair, which is braided in thin braids that are parted the center of his head and flow down to about his jawline. He always has a 4 o'clock shadow on his face. He's fair skinned. In the ring, he wears black wrestling boots, small style tights, the speedo-esque ones, that are green, with a shamrock on it. The back reads 'O'HARA'. He wear torn blue jean shorts to the ring, but take them off right before the match starts.

The O'Hara's were a fighting family in the poor sectors of the Irish hood in Boston. They were the offspring of poor Irish immigrants, and were raised to appreciate hard work and the rewards that it can bring. All the O'Hara's were streetfighters, and in were involved in organized crime for a spell. Evenutally, they got out and turned to Professional Wrestling for their main source of income. Brody is the strikes it out in singles competition, looking to one day become the UWF World Heavyweight Champion.

caption: The O'Hara family's own hardcore all-rounder, managing Ash O'Hara and allied with Bowie O'Hara and the Red Reefers alike.

name: Bruce Gordy

tenures.finisher: Painful Innovation — Mix between a pumphandle slam, but then into a piledriver
tenures.bio:
1 Time (T)he (H)ardcore (C)hampionship

Bruce Gordy is a vey sadistic and extreme man. He is a hardcore specialist. He is dressed as a hardcore butcher but he is much more than just a wrestling gimmick. He is called the Innovator of Pain because he craves the feeling of inflicting pain on others and even himself. He is also called the Sole Survivor of the Elements of Destruction. The EoD was the greatest stable ever assembled. It started in GIWF with The Plague, TNT (Tommy N. Taylor), and Killer Dude. Then it grew a little and Bruce Gordy joined and later came Digital Mortality and Toxic Shock. But the first version was with Plague, TNT, Killer Dude, and Bruce Gordy. Gordy was a top contender in the GIWF for the THC and Television championships although he never suceeded in winning them. He feuded against Mike Montgomery and fought him in the famous cage match at the 3 STrikes and You're Out PPV. He infamously powerbombed Montgomery off the top of the cage. The EoD would continue to live on in different reincarnations like with Ian Thorn and Corrupt Judgment, but then Bruce Gordy returned and entered the UWF after a few years of silence. Bruce Gordy restarted the EoD with Killer Dude and Plague and Kevin Starr joined. He tried to get Jamie Shock formely known as Toxic Shock but he refused. Bruce Gordy feuded with Mike Montgomery affter Montgomery refused his friendship offer. It was nominated for feud of the year but the awards hve not been released yet so we'll just have to see if we won. The EoD got to the finals of Stable Wars 5 but were beaten evenutally by the worst stable ever with DJ Cool, Montgomery, and Wimp and Chimp Connection. Bruce Gordy would disappear eventually after the defeat but came back and won his life long goal of a championship when he won the THC title from Beelzebozo. Eventually Ben Jericho beat Gordy for the title, but now Bruce Gordy is still out there ready to inflict pain and win back his THC belt.

tenures.finisher: Mask Your Affection — Mask stands on the opponent's face, trying to balance for as long as he can, which puts extreme pressure on the opponent's head. Once the balancing is through, he drops sumo-style on the opponent's head and calls for the cover, hooking the opponent's legs behind him.
tenures.bio:
Appearance: Hot Mask is never seen without his...you guessed it...mask. A bright red and sparkly head disguise with a large white flame emblem that covers the face (save for the eyes and mouth holes.) Mask's build is very trimmed and lean, with noticable muscle tone that doesn't bear too much muscle mass. Skin is always lightly tanned and hairless, regardless of what time of year. Ring attire consists of his mask, a pair of matching bright red full-length tights with a white exclamation point design over the crotch area, standard white wrestling boots with an old-school 'HM' in red on the sides of the boots, and standard white elbow pads.

Biography: Being 19 years old, you would think that an individual would have grown out of childish insults and catcalling, as well as being completely spoiled rotten and self-absorbed. Think again. Hot Mask is about as obnoxious as they come, with an ego that could make hot air balloons cower in fear and a tongue that could make a sailor blush. Taking male chauvenism to it's utmost extreme, Hot Mask is downright degrading, lewd, and immature when it comes to women, and is the antithesis of political correctness. Could also be accused of homophobia, but tends to have a somewhat homoerotic intimidation technique while wrestling in the ring.

Despite his immaturity, Hot Mask is as crafty as a 30-year veteran when it comes to his ringwork. A mastermind at bending the rules and getting off scot-free, it is a rarity that he wins a match with a clean pinfall. It's near impossible for Hot Mask to have any fans, because hell...even complete assholes think this guy is a jerk. Add a somewhat squeaky voice and cockroach-type bounciness...and you've got a total package of grossly perverted and self-worshipping talent.

As far as background goes, Caleb Mason is a relative unknown in the wrestling world. Wrestling in independents around the Kentucky area with virtually no gimmick whatsoever, Mason decided to seek higher ground. After much plotting, the character of Hot Mask was born.

Entering the budding young organization run by Pierre Hyde, Neon Wrestling, Mask debuted and quickly became widely despised by the roster, management, and fans alike.  Maintaining a flawless record, he was given a shot at the No-Holds-Barred title held by 'Sensational' Sean White, and defeated him...but the victory was in vain, as Neon Wrestling came to a close that night due to managerial problems.  Mask proceeded to pack his bags and pawn the belt for a rare black market porno tape, and make his way to the Ultimate Wrestling Federation, where he currently resides.

Manager: Skankalie

Manager Description: Don't take Skankalie's name to heart, because to the eye she is anything but wretched. A very beautiful girl with short blonde hair and extremely cute facial features (think: a spitting image of Brittany Daniel from the movie Joe Dirt). However, by some strange force, she is completely under the control of Hot Mask. Forced to wear nothing but a potato sack to accompany him to his matches, and strapped to his side by a leash and collar, she is degraded on a consistant basis by the cocky young wrestler. Carries with her a loaded purse that often conceals some odd foreign object that Mask takes advantage of during matches.

name: Iron Lung

tenures.finisher: The Iron Lung — Pedigree setup, lifts opponent over shoulders and pancakes them face first into the mat
tenures.bio:
Growing up on the streets is always hard, and that's exactly what the young IL did. He was abandoned as a child with no collection of who he was or who his parents were, he made a dark alleyway his home for his childhood. He lived in a cardboard box next to drunken bums in an area which cops always kept under close watch, there was gang warfare at every turn on this turf. One day would live with him the rest of his life and it would change his view of life for a long time to come...

Awakened by the calls of 'fight', Lung was oh so curious as to what was going on. Lung walked playfully to this large circle with children and what he saw shocked him, a fight was going on between two children and one was obviously getting beat to a bloddy pulp. The person who beat the other child laughed and scared off the rest of the children, but Lung stayed put not knowing what to do. The child turned out to be the neighborhood bully Johnny Rico, he shoved Lung and laughed while Lung stayed put. Rico shoved Lung to the ground and thats when the children came back out and noticed that Lung had snapped, Lung started fighting Rico back and then kneed Rico in the gut giving him a hard slam onto the cement knocking Rico out cold. The children came out and cheered, Rico had been defeated and needed paramedics to put him on an 'Iron Lung' so he could get back to breathing normally, that's how Iron Lung got his name...

Over the years Lung became an awesome fighter, he competed in neighborhood competitions and eventually one the Neighborhood Fight Championship. After nine years of neighborhood fights, Lung decided to leave Norwalk and persue a real wrestling career. At the young age of eleven he started to train in the Lion's Den Wrestling Dojo under the supervision of Master Jade, the grown men all laughed at this youngster they were all in their teens. Lung was determined to prove them all wrong and at the end of his two years training there was a tournament which Lung entered hoping to become the Dojo Champion. Lung defeated all oncomers and won the Championship, Jade told him he had learned everything he could at the Dojo and now it was time to persue a real wrestling career. Today Iron Lung continues to thrill us all in the sport that he considers his home...

tenures.bio:
Growing up the only child of two
prominent NYC Defense Attorneys, J.D. was able to ge
the finest of anything that he had ever wanted. He
was sent to the finest private schools that money
could afford. In those very schools is where the
foundation of his future would be cemented. 

In those schools he learned everything that would
help him as he grew older. But he also learned
things that were not found in any textbook he read.
He learned that because of who his parents were and
the lifestyle his family lived, he could basically
get away with anything he wanted. He abused this
priviledge all his life, buying his way out of
trouble with other children, the schools, and even
the police. Everything was going fine until his
parents discovered his secret.
 
One afternoon his parents walked in on him and few
of his friends snorting lines of cocaine in their
living room. His parents disowned him and forced him
out on his own. Having nowhere to go and the little
money his parents actually gave him before he left,
he rented a room in a middle class hotel and began
selling cocaine to make money. Soon he was able to
afford his own apartment overlooking Times Square
and he figured he'd once again become invincible. 
 
In August of 2000, J.D. was arrested in an
undercover sting by the NYPD for distribution of a
controlled substance. He was sentenced to six years
in prison but was parolled after three for good
behavior. He decided to change his life, he wanted
to do something that was legal and at the same time
very phsyical. One day he was walking down Broadway
and noticed a flyer for a wrestling school. He
joined the school and left one of the best students
who had been through there in a while. His next move
was to head to the big time.
catchphrases: Damn, I thought you knew. I'm just that much better than you.

name: Jamie Shock

tenures.finisher: The Lynch — Grabs opponents neck from behind, jumps into the air, then crashes down to the mat on his knees, almost snapping the opponents neck in a modified neck braker
tenures.bio:
He did it all.

Entered the UWF as a rookie, as Toxic Shock, with his girlfriend, and hoped of just 'making it OK' as a normal, average, superstar.

He ended up being, possibly, the most hated man in UWF history.

How? ..I mean.. look back in the summer of 2001.. and the start of 2002.. he was a fan favourite. He was a man with a plan.

Greed.

After only accomplishing the tv and tag team titles after a year.. he left. He was retired - then he came back.

He won all the titles he had been unable to win in the short space of 4 weeks.

Then.. then he got beat by a Chimp. He lost the World Title to a chimp.

..of course, that wasnt the end. He returned, still a crazed mad man.. became the new commissioner.. then started swinging his crowbar at his enimies like a butcher cutting up his meat.

He cost Seymour Almasy the world title to his *only friend* Ruff Ryder. Then he invited Malcolm Kennedy, a young rookie, to join himself and Ryder in 'The Prime Alliance' before mysteriously dissapearing.

Then months later he returned again, a changed man. Wanting to right the wrongs, his first target is Malcolm Kennedy; a cocky trash talker, who has done nothing but stab knifes into Jamie's back since he left.

tenures.bio: Born on September 16, 1972 in Detroit, Michigan. John Williams, aka Jonny Roxx, was just one piece of a large puzzle that was his family. His parents both held two jobs to support their seven children, the youngest being John. When John was seven years old he was introduced to a band called Led Zeppelin. He immediately fell in love with rock music. He went further and discovered bands like Aerosmith, The Who, and KISS. When he turned fourteen and many hair metal bands were striking big, John decided to start his own rock band, Love Fist. When he was sixteen the band actually was signed to a record deal and they were big in the Vice City area. Williams, who now changed his name to Jonny Roxx, was a great singer and it lead to great popularity. But a few years later when the grunge scene came about, Love Fist disbanded and Roxx was out of a job. He tried to lead many more bands, but the hair metal style just wasn't popular anymore. Now, about 13 years after his only successful musical stint, he is back to start over once again but one thing is standing in his way.....he has no money.

name: Joshua Dunn

tenures.finisher: The Ten Dunn Salute — Dunn picks up the opponent in a firemans carry, flips them round and holds them upside down and places a foot over their chin, then drives their head into the floor up to ten times, sometimes the crowd even count along
tenures.bio:
Before the UWF Joshua was a Junior Highland Games Champion, and came to the UWF in the early months of the fed.after a short spell of nothing spectacular, Dunn was kidnapped by the Local NVA Company and brainwashed to carry out their evil bidding and thus becoming a communist and never being able to overcome those drugs the NVA used on him.  Shortly afterwards He won the shoot title off of Mike montgomery in the first ever written match of the UWF (i think).  After getting screwed out of Stable wars for the first time, Dunn didn't do much, appart from a feud with kevin starr who held the THC title at the time, in a title vs. title match up, Kevign ended up the shot champion and Dunn the THC Champion and after a spell of time i don't remember that well (including trying to turn BBB against state trooper roger rogers, which almost worked) left the fed.

Returning in the build up to the next stable wars under the banner of the Prime Alliance (ugh) he joined the side of Digital Mortality again along with Jamie Shock and Ruff Ryder, getting screwed out of his second consecutive Stable Wars.  After that time Dunn went on to win the IC title for the first time in a ladder cage match against Kevin Starr and Mike Montgomery inserting himself in the match by kidnapping Starr's nephew.  Going to prison for that, he was leater released by Mike Montgomery, he joined him all that time ago to become the Players Club.  soon, somehow, he came across Digital Mortality's woman who had left him some time ago, inraging his former partner and creating a bitter feud between the two escalating into a fight for the IC title which Digital Won.  Not long afterwards, using Justine as leverage, Joshua entered against Digital Mortality for the IC title and won, and sending digital out of the fed for a few moths, apparantly never to be seen again.

No one ever took the IC title off of Dunn in the next 140 days, not even the once great Seymour Almasy, Which Dunn won in the Mount Gagazet II deatmatch.  After Beating Almasy in his own stipulation, Dunn then vacated the title in search of better things.

The Players Club lay dormant for a while, as with Mike Montgomery gone, no one knowing where, He was left in charge of the Club, and a newer form of the Prime Alliance reformed and started their campaign to be the best damn stable in the UWF.  After Recruiting Ezra, the long forgotten Players Club was thrust back into the lime light as the only teaming able to combat the Prime Alliance.  With Mike returned and Joshua at the helm, They waged a war agains thte Prime Alliance which finalised on one SAS with a three part main event, seeing the Players Club white wash the Prime alliance 3-0, and the disgraced Jamie Shock left the federation.

After a spell of having no competition what so ever, holdng the IC title and Tag title's the players Club really did reign supreme, until the return of Digital Mortality and Moraless who swore they would dismantle the UWF and rebuild it again.  Not going to allow this to happen, a new battle was waged, this time between the Players Club and the Ressurection.  losing all their collective gold, and gaining the World Title, thanks to Mike Montgomery, the Players Club seemed in trouble, especially when Resurrection member #3 was introduced as Bondage the Sex Fiend.  Dunn brought it upon himself to disgrace the Resurrection and stop their gloating by way of the Dunn Exhibition Gauntlet, a Hardcore Match, followed by a submissions match, followed by a last man standing match, against the entire Resurection.  Only a draw was managed against the Scotsman as he won 1, lost one, and drew one.

This tit for tat escalated into Stable Wars VI, where both the Resurrection and The Players Club made it to the Finals, Digital, Moraless, Bondage the Sex Fiend and Malcolm Kenedy, against Joshua Dunn, Ezra Kazee Kevin Starr and Nick Persia.  Of course the wild card of the match was Richard Ray Vaugn's Super Squadron (or whatever they were called) and this came down to just Digitla Mortality and Joshua Dunn.  Dunn finally managing to over come past difficulties and beat Digital to win his first Stable Wars (and screwing Digital out of his third).  His victory stunted as the KnightMare Brigade stormed in on his celebrations and publicly humiliated him, shaving off all his hair and gluing a mop to his head.  Dunn vowed revenge against them after having the mop surgically removed from his head, leaving it horribly scarred, and no he volutarily wears head bandages to keep it out of sight of the public.

name: Kevin Starr

tenures.finisher: Superstarr Slam — Kevin puts his opponent in Powerbomb position with head in between legs. Then lifts him up as if he's going for a Powerbomb, then when his opponent reaches his shoulders, he pushes out on their legs away from his body so the opponent is looking straing down at the mat in air. Then he grabs his opponents head in mid air and brings him down for an X-Factor like move.
tenures.bio:
Kevin Starr was born awesome. I mean, just look at how many wins he has in his record on the UWF website. Simply Awesome! Kevin Starr discovered his awesomeness somewhere around the age of 3, when he first discovered his talent for juggling brownies. After that he took off. Becoming more awesome, and more awesome everyday. 

Growing up in school, he earned the nickname, Kevin 'Awesome' Starr. That's how awesome he was. He ruled the hallways, strutting by the other kids who would envy him and whisper 'Someday, I wish I could be as awesome as him'

Kevin Starr was a natural at being awesome. So awesome, he called all the non awesome kids, emosewa, which is awesome backwards. Kevin Starr was in no way a bully though, he would give the emosewa's 3 seconds to empty their pockets full of money before he pounded them. Unlike the others who simply pounded them, THEN asked for their money. Buttholes is what they were.

After a few years in school, Kevin 'Awesome' Starr got tired of the bullies beating up the emosewa's. So he got all the emosewa's together and started a Revolution against the bullies of the school... of course at a small price of the emosewa's lunch money.

But soon enough, after over 7 minutes of intense training, Kevin led all of 500 emosewa's to the playground after school to face the bullies who were already waiting. The emosewa's had at least 300 kids over the bullies. It was a stare down at first, the bullies standing on one side of the playground, the emosewa's standing on the other, with Kevin out in front. Not a sound was heard, the only movement was that of a ball of tumbleweed rolling across the pavement in between the two armies. Then, Kevin turns to his emosewa's and gave a speech, to hopefully motivate them...

'Listen up! Just look out there... look at THEM! Look at their fat, dirty, brainless heads! For years they have been stealing your lunch money, stealing your homework, throwing you in trash bins, and breaking your pencils. They have gotten the best of you for FAR TOO LONG! It's time to put your foot down and show them that doing all of those things is wrong! That you are not their plaything! That you are all tired of their bullying! Now let's show them that you to have fists of your own! CHAAAAARRRGGGEE!!!'

And with that, Kevin 'Awesome' Starr raised his arm, pointing at the bullies as emosewa after emosewa ran past him, charging straight towards the bullies and even though heavily out numbered, running straight toward the emosewa's!

After a few seconds of pointless fighting, every single last emosewa lay on the ground in heavy pain, as the bullies walk around the battlefield asking each of the emosewa's for their leftover lunch money.

Kevin Starr stands at the edge of the playground and shrugs... well at least he tried.

Well anyway, Kevin Starr learned a very important lesson after this. He not only learned that emosewa's can't fight, but that he is not only awesome but... REALLY awesome. Kevin's awesomeness level only went up from there as he graduated school and got into the wrestling business.

tenures.bio:
Born August 22nd, 1976, Kyle Cross was an exceptional athlete throughout his childhood, and a junior hockey sensation in his teens, destined for the NHL. In 1992, be began playing for the Calgary Hitmen  of the Western Hockey League, a team partially owned by wrestler Bret Hart. Cross played well in Calgary, and widely became known as one of the strongest and fastest wingers in the game.  A year later, and Cross was already being talked about for the NHL Draft, and after declaring that he was ready to go up to the NHL, speculation ran wild that he would be the number one pick overall. However, just one month before the draft, Cross was injured in a motorcycle accident in Ottawa. Surgery was required, and the knee was reconstructed.  He missed the draft, a fact that devastated him emotionally. Facing months of rehab to his damaged left knee, he felt totally alone. It was during this time that Cross was contacted by Bret Hart, who offered a alternative to straight medical rehabilitation.  It turns out that a student at the wrestling school run by two of Brets brothers had just undergone similar surgery, and Bret suggested that Kyle come to Calgary and the two men could work out together.  Cross agreed and flew back to Calgary.

During the fall and winter of '94-'95, Kyle Cross and John J. Nightside (the injured wrestling student) went from rehabbing their injuries into full-out wrestling training, joining up with The Hart Brothers Wrestling School that spring.  Everyone was surprised at how quickly Kyle picked up the sport, and quickly adapted to the Canadian submission style that the Hart Brothers taught.  In September 1995, Bruce Hart worked out a deal that would send Kyle, John and other students from the school on a six-month exchange to New Japan Pro Wrestling for six months while several junior NJPW superstars would come to Calgary to train at the school.

Upon arriving in Japan, the bookers in NJPW suggested that Cross don a mask.  Cross agreed, creating The Dark Spyder persona.  He participated in many NJPW matches, and during the fall and winter of 1995 worked with some of the best wrestlers in the world, including Ric Flair, Sting, Shinya Hashimoto, and a man who would play a very important role later in his career Keiji Muto.  In the end though, the six month exchange was coming to a close, and it looked like Cross would end up returning to Canada and signing with a small, indy promotion.  Then he got a phone call from Atsushi Onita.

Atsushi Onita, widely viewed as the father of modern extreme, liked The Dark Spyder, and wanted to sign Cross to an extended contract with his FMW promotion.  Cross agreed and was introduced to the brutal world of deathmatch wrestling.  During those years, Cross (still known as The Dark Spyder) worked with an eclectic cast of characters, including Onita, Mr. Pogo, Hayabusa, The Gladiator Mike Awesome, Masato Tanaka and others.

T.D.S. quickly developed a following in Japan, bouncing back and forth between 'garbage' promotions like FMW & Big Japan and national promotions like AJPW, NJPW & NOAH.  He eventually lost the mask and became known as 'The Guardian Angel' Kyle Cross.  Again, he enjoyed considerable success. Yet Kyle was always looking for the opportunity to cross over to a North American wrestling audience.  It would take nearly a decade of barbed wire and spilled blood before the opportunity presented itself.

On January 15th, 2004...  The Universal Wrestling Federation  held TERROR IN TOKYO - REGAL RUMBLE FIVE.  The main event was a 60-Man Rumble event.  Promoters wanted to use some local puroresu talent in the Rumble, and contacted Cross, who by this time had become a true hardcore legend in Japan, and one of the most popular gajin wrestlers in the country.  Cross realized that although it was originally set up to be a one time appearance, if he could impress UWF officials and fans in the Rumble, they would have no choice but to offer him a contract.

name: Misfit

tenures.finisher: Stigmata — A fisherman DDT.
tenures.bio:
One of the most well-travelled men in the busines, Misfit has done it all.

His pre-wrestling life is virtually non-existant in documentation, the only scraps available are his birth certificate (born in Seattle, Washington to a single mother) and his high school diploma (he graduated near the top of his class, though none of his schoolmates seem to remember him).

His career began at the age of 18 with little to no training. Thus, like many others, he turned to the American garbage scene and quickly established himself as a god amongst the hardcore cicuits. For a couple of years he would travel the country, learning the wrestling basics from the trained wrestlers he stepped into the ring with night after night.

In 1997, Misfit decided to leave the wrestling world for a short time to recieve more in-depth training. He once again packed up his van and travelled the country, spending various amounts of time at the best schools money could buy.

He would reimerge towards the end of the year to begin dominating the west coast indie scene, wracking up a near flawless win/loss record and several championships. Even with his training, his passion for American hardcore could not be tamed and he soon began to balance his appearances on the west coast indies with runs in the biggest garbage feds in the country.

1999 brought about Misfit's first run with a major company, pulling him out of the indie and garbage feds and into the homes of the average American wrestling fan. The critics loved his ring psychology and charism, though his lack of variety in style caused him to falter. After failing to draw as he was expected, the company let Misfit go and he soon seemed to disappear once again.

In early-2002, Misfit seemingly rose from the dead to join the UWF roster. He claimed to have travelled the wrestling world during his absence, though no documents were available to prove his claims. His in-ring performance, however, told the story differently. Not soon to forget, the backlash was near-immediate as his presence in the hotshot fed was heavily protested.

Upon being given a chance to shine in the ring, however, the critics swiftly changed their tune. Misfit has since become a figurehead of the UWF, claiming almost every prize available and continuing to impress everyone with his innovative, unmatched style. He blends every possible style of wrestling together almost seamlessly with his excellent psychology, and continues to deliver mindblowing, charismatic promos.

Having paid his dues, its now just a matter of time before Misfit finally has his time.

name: Pájaro de Presa

entrance_music.verbatim: April 23, 1981 (Alleged, his 'birth certificate' was handwritten on a Jack-in-the-Box napkin)

tenures.finisher: Phoenix Splash — 450 Splash
tenures.bio:
Description: Hair color: Black (presumed) 
Eye Color: Brown 
Fill in the rest of the details: Pájaro de Presa has a slender but athletic build, well-defined and very little body fat. He is lightly tanned and appears to have long, black hair. However, the color has been known to change to shades of white and green, leading some to theorize that it's a wig attached to his mask. His mouth is still visible, and runs constantly. 

Attire: Pájaro de Presa typically wears baggy black pants that resemble part of a karate gi. He wrestles shirtless with bizarre gloves or arm wrappings that look more like something seen in a goth club than a wrestling ring. His mask quite ornate, having various points that give it an avian look. The material is usually of a fancy design or metallic look.

Resembles: Juventud Guerrera

Gimmick: VERY cocky. He's prone to talking to fans, calling out the names of his moves, and pausing for effect. He also likes doing that 'pretend to blow snot on your downed opponent' bit that Benoit used to do. Before hitting the Death From Above, he holds his arms out wide, then crosses his hands over his chest, linking his thumbs so his hands make a sort of bird symbol, then leaps, spreading his arms again before connecting with his victim. He also likes to kick his foe a few times, get them staggering, flip them the 'Bird,' then floor them with another kick, like the spinning inferno. As a true rudo, Pájaro de Presa is more than willing to give another man a boot to the cajones if it will get him the win. 

History: Very little is known about Pájaro de Presa, which roughly translates to 'Bird of Prey.' He hails from Cancun, which might explain his irreverent attitude. Pajaro de Presa is the 'Rudo with Attitude-o.' Manic and flamboyant, he seems to have a better grasp on wrestling than he does on reality. He sees himself as an unbeatable luchador and an irrefutable ladies' man. He brushes off any attempts to find out about his past. He has never been seen without his mask. How he was trained, where he gained his experience, what his true goals are ... all are unknown. Which is just how Pájaro de Presa likes it.

tenures.bio:
Reod started in the small community of Morristown, MN. A population of 800 people 
was not his idea of a party place. He moved to Minneapolis at the age of 16 
where he started to hang with a rough crowd. Here he learned the anything goes style 
of Pit Fighting. At age 17, Joanna entered his life. She liked what she saw and started 
to manage his career. For 2 years they traveled the country, winning match after match. 
Then it all ended on fateful night. Reod was slammed on his knee on the cement floor. His 
Knee was shattered, and so was his career. The next year, he was to spend in rehab, he 
told Joanna to continue her career. All through the year, Reod could thing of nothing but 
making a comeback. Joanna would keep him up to date on her life, including the new 
Tag Team she had in Pro Wrestling. Then one day, She came to him with an offer. One 
member of her team had retired. Joanna wanted Reod to fill his spot. He agreed on one 
condition. No other allies. From that moment on Anarchy was Born.

tenures.bio:
Robb Daniels was born on May 29th of 1980. The sibling/brother of former MPW Superstar and Tag Team Champion Eric Daniels. He grew up in the small metropolitan area of Lexington, Kentucky. Robb and Eric's childhood friends were former MPW Superstar Sean Ryan, and fellow MPW Superstar Jason Todd also known as Jefferson. They all four were vivid fans of Wrestling. As Young childeren they would watch it regulary, and pretend they were pro wrestlers. Having no knowledge that someday in there future, that actually would be there career. 
They attended Lookout Elementary, then moved on to Millard High School, they graduated from the consolidated school of East Ridge High. They attended the University of Kentucky, Robb then met his future wife but at the time girl friend Felicia Daniels. 

Robb Daniels broke into the Wrestling Scene with Jefferson in the FWEn. In his Sports Entertainment Debut he defeated Hot Ice for the FWEn United States Championship. Later the invasion of WCWE standing for World Championship Wrestling Extreme, Robb Daniels the FWEn U.S. Champion and Jefferson the newly crowned FWEn World Champion jumped ships to the WCWE side. They then demolished there respected titles on WCWE programming. 

After the demise of FWEn they completely focused there careers on WCWE, Robb became the first ever WCWE Champion. But then a week later after his Championship win, he was then stripped for a Draft for 2 different shows...Monday Night Nitro, and Thursday Night Thunder, Thunder had the first pick, and chose Jefferson because the General Manager was Hulk Hogan and he wasn't to fond of Robb Daniels. Robb was then the 2nd pick to Monday Night Nitro to the General Manager of Ric Flair. That Night they crowned each shows individual Champion, and Robb Daniels then won the WCWE Championship yet again for the Second time. Then Nitro General Manager Ric Flair was dramaticly injured in a car accident and was preceeded as General Manager by Stephanie McMahon. Soon after Robb Daniels lost the titles to friend Sean Ryan, and then Sean Ryan lost the title to friend Eric Daniels. Jefferson on Thunder was having success also as the Television Champion but they each got together and quit WCWE and went to WWE. 

Now in WWE, Robb Daniels and Jefferson find there selves in the title hunt as Sean Ryan and Eric Daniels are in search on Tag Team Gold. Jefferson and Robb were in a Tag Match and then Jefferson turned on Robb starting a feud imediately between the 2. Later they were at the WWE PPV Summerslam in the Retribution Chamber and Robb Daniels eliminated Jefferson and was at the top of the cage with Kez trying to reach the gold, but then Sean Ryan shows up throws Kez to the second cage then Memory shows up and throws Robb from the top cage thru the 2nd then thru the 1st and he laid almost dead inside the ring. Robb and Jefferson both cheated out of the Title hunt, found singles succes Robb winning the Intercontinental Championship, and Jefferson with the United States Championship, near the end of WWE they had a match to bring the titles together and Robb Daniels came out victorious winning both titles and being rewarded the ner WWE International Championship title belt. Then they left and went to the CWEF. 

Now Robb and Jefferson together again past there differences they thought won the CWEF Tag Team Championships right off the bat a record setting 9 times. Robb won the CWEF World Championship from Red Man, and the from Razor. After there short but glorious time in CWEF they were invited to Dare 2 Dream and Robb and Jefferson's heat started again, with Robb Daniels vs. Jefferson for the D2D Championship, with Robb prevailing. They then changed the name to MPW where they are currently at now. 
Finally in the Prime part of there career Robb Daniels bouts himself in many battles against the More Power Wrestling Champion Jefferson. Robb the crowd favorite and Jefferson the hated Rival have had many great matches with eachother, as well as against eachother, but now it's more importantly for the World Championship of MPW can Robb get it done, the furture can only tell us. Robb Daniels aligns himself with Sean Ryan, his brother Eric Daniels and newfound friend Mark Miller to make the remarkable force of the 'Natural Born Thrillers'! 

Later Down the Road in MPW, the Natural Born Thriller's wouldn't last with it crumbling, by Sean and Eric losing the Tag Titles and Mark Miller coming down with an illness, Robb took off on his own and competed for the MPW World Title against Jefferson in many matchs but to no evail was cheated and robbed of the World Title each time. At the December Pay-Per-View, Robb fit in the first ever MPW Elimination Chamber Match with 5 other competitors, he was the last of 2 Men and was eliminated by Annihilator and suffered a leg injury and had a MRI the following day and the doctor did not clear him to wrestle. So out of action for a unknown amount of time, Jamez turned to Robb Daniels and asked him to become the new MPW Fire General Manager, and Robb did. 

For 3 Consecutive Weeks Robb Daniels, made Friday Night Fire the highlight of the week, with First Ever Gauntlet Match, and a Buried Alive Match. And helped an old friend leave MPW in style. He then formed the faction known as 'Evolution'. Robb and Jefferson had reunited and were looking good on there own until MPW mysteriously shut down for a while. But on the 2nd week of January MPW was back, with a new show called Tuesday Night Titans. Robb Daniels then made his return defeating 4 people to win the vacant MPW Extreme Title, his first taste of MPW Gold, and then in the next Match Robb and Jefferson defeated the MPW Tag Team Champions and won the titles. Now Robb Daniels is the first ever Double-Champion in MPW. But later that week on Friday they were screwed out of the titles, by Team Zoo. Robb and Jefferson then welcomed the MPW Champion Annihilator, and the new 50% Owner of MPW Dustin into Evolution to take on No Remorse. 

Shortly After Dustin and some of the MPW Roster had a fallen out and he quit. He didn't show up for the MPW Roster Split and I Robb Daniels was declared the new 50% Owner of MPW and General Manager of Fire. Once Fire GM I brought in some of the best talent to the Fire Brand. I brought Nyne back and brought Dustin in to be the Fire Chief of Staff. Annihilator was then part of Evolution and lost the title to Jefferson, and then Robb handed over his Tag Title Belt to Annihilator to defend with Jefferson on a Full-Time Basis. I lost the Extreme Championship to a great person being Tenacious D. Later on in the upcoming weeks Tenacious D declared his retirement of injury and wrestled his last Match on Fire and lost his Extreme Title to Seymour Boner. They had a Retirement Part after Fire went of the Air. Robb then declared himself the US Champion then handed it over to Nyne when he beat Remedy Punk. The Roster Split wasn't working out because someone was hacking MPW and had major beef with Jefferson, Robb and Jamez. So Jefferson quit MPW while MPW Champion.

The Downfall of MPW was about to begin, so all members of Evolution has now quit, Robb and Jefferson find themselves signing with Universal Wrestling Federation.  The Tandem of Robb Daniels and Jefferson has been through it all, FWENCWEFWCWEWWE.D2DMPW.and Now onto there next obstacle PWF!  Now Robb has found himself in a hard situation and only the future will tell what lies ahead for Robb Daniels and his EVOLUTION!

tenures.note: First seen is the Ultratitle Preseason of 30 May 2005, where NFW's own roster links first carry him; last seen is his last mention, on Crash TV 47, 15 March 2009. THE FED'S OWN RECORD NOW STATES BOTH A DEBUT AND A DEPARTURE. The debut is the Ultratitle Preseason of 30 May 2005 itself: its “The Final Fantasy Interview” (matchseg 47834) is an ESEN “NFW: ATHLETE PROFILE” introducing him as “one of the many newcomers to the NFW scene”, rolling clips of his All-Star Championship Wrestling matches, and he answers in his own voice — “I’m Seymour Almasy. I’m 5’7”, 181 pounds, and I’m twenty-four years old. I’ve been wrestling for about two years now”. The departure is stated on Crash TV 47 of 15 March 2009, in the fed’s own commentary during the Sears Tower Television Title match (matchseg 48008), as Impulse re-applies the leglock he beat him with: “H’WOOD: And we never saw Almasy again.” NFW's own late-2006 power rankings place him seventh among the promotion's notables (promotions/nfw/archive/nfw-playoffs.html). The fed's own roleplay board carries his name too, not only its show archive: its own thread index lists three threads bearing his name, none captured by Wayback — thread 12302, "Week 4: Seymour Almasy vs. Lindsay Troy" (forum 163, THE VAULT: RP Archives), corroborating Crash TV 30 (9 Oct 2005, Lindsay Troy vs Seymour Almasy); thread 12648, "Week 6: N. Quiry vs. Seymour Almasy" (same forum), corroborating Midnight Madness 6 (1 Jan 2006, Almasy vs. N. Quiry); and thread 14661, "The Impending Demise of Seymour Almasy" (same forum), naming a storyline the served show corpus does not otherwise carry. All three are checked negatives, not unchecked gaps — each was probed exact and non-collapsed against showthread.php?t=<id>, showthread.php?<id>-Slug, archive/index.php/t-<id>.html and printthread.php?t=<id>, and every probe returned empty. The standing bio.php?username=almasy re-probe is also now closed, honestly negative: a non-collapsed prefix census of nfw.e-wrestling.org/bio.php (and the www. variant) returns the fed's own bio cards in urlkey order — …?username=alexander, then …?username=anderson — and almasy sorts between them and is absent; the page existed, the crawl never took it. HIS OWN BIO CARD IS NOW IN HAND, from the federation’s own backstage database rather than from the web: bio 10806, charactername “almasyDEATH”, 22 populated fields, the card this tenure’s billing fields are now taken from. The Wayback gap above is unchanged and stays recorded as what it is — the page existed and the crawl never took it; what has changed is that the card’s own content survives elsewhere. The card is also a second, independent receipt that almasyDEATH is Almasy: one roster row holds both personas, the masked 2008 billing sitting on the same bio as the 2005 Season 2 run, beside the fed’s own Wrestlestock II commentary this record already cites. Its Alias field reads “The Final Fantasy”; its Other Feds field, in voice, “Oy. Not enough room here to list them all.”; its Other Fed Titles “Lots. Take my word for it.”; and its Other Fed Awards “Ditto. You really don’t want to read them, so I’ll spare y’all the time.” Three card fields with no home in this shape are kept here: blood type AB+, eye colour green, trainer “Unknown”. THE FED’S OWN APPEARANCE RECORD: 24 rows over 14 cards, 30 May 2005 to 15 June 2008 — twelve matches and twelve segments. Five wins by its own grading (Lennox Love, Midnight Madness 2; Azala Zameer, Midnight Madness 3; Lindsay Troy, Crash TV 30; Uriel, Midnight Madness 5; Troy Windham, Midnight Madness 7), five losses (Rook Black, Midnight Madness 1; Kodiak Vic Creed, WRESTLESTOCK I; Lindsay Troy, Midnight Madness 11; the Television Title Battle Royal, WRESTLESTOCK II; Impulse, Crash TV 45) and one graded n/a (the Divisional Demolition Derby of Midnight Madness 11). ONE ROW OF THE FED’S OWN THIS RECORD DECLINES: matchseg 47739 grades him a Loss in “Tom Adler vs. Guy Boudreaux”, a bout he was not a competitor in — Midnight Madness 11 ran its Demolition Derby as concurrent threads through one arena, and its text has him hunting the weapon cache and taking a shotgun blast from Craig Miles while Adler and Boudreaux wrestle, so the appearance is real and the LOSS is a bracket artifact. It is carried here as part of his Midnight Madness 11 segment presence and never as a sixth defeat. THE FINISHER HAS A NAME OF ITS OWN: ULTIMA IX. Lindsay Troy beats him with it at Midnight Madness 11 (matchseg 47114) — “She’s calling for the ULTIMA IX! That’s the move ALMASY used to defeat her in their first encounter during Week 4” — Week 4 being Crash TV 30 of 9 October 2005, the win this record already carries. TWO NIGHTS THE FED’S OWN RECORD SETTLES. At WRESTLESTOCK I (20 April 2006, matchseg 47925) its own appearance rows grade him a Loss and Kodiak Vic Creed a Win, which closes a winner this wing’s show row could previously only infer from a later commentary line. At WRESTLESTOCK II (20 April 2008, matchseg 47257) the Television Title Battle Royal is a title defence on the fed’s own title table — title 130, the NFW Television Championship, champion before and after Joe the Plumber — and Jason Payne threw him out to leave the final five, the fed’s own call crediting Steve Knox with him: “PAYNE THROWS ALMASY OUT OF THE RING! … STEVE KNOX AND JASON PAYNE ELIMINATED ALMASY!” THE CARD’S BIRTHDAY FIELD IS THE CHARACTER’S BILLED AGE, NOT A PERSON’S, AND SERVES. It reads “Exact date unknown, roughly 23-24 years old.” The ESEN profile above has the character say the same number in his own voice on the fed’s own show — “I’m twenty-four years old” — and his own cards in three other federations give the character a kayfabe birthday in 1981 (12 June 1981 in Sin City Championship Wrestling and Global Championship Wrestling, 3 July 1981 in PRIME), which is exactly the age the 2005 card states and is not the age of the man who wrote him. It is in-character billing under #privacy’s own organising principle, and it would serve regardless under the memorial exemption.

tenures.note: First seen in PRIME's segments of 14 September 2005 (ReVolution 75), attacking Karina Wolfenden as a GCW star ahead of PTC's Super Series; seen again at ReVolution 108 (13 October 2006), billed by its commentary as the reigning PTC Global Champion, and at ReVolution 110 (8 November 2006), charging the ring after Rich Rollins. Found in the King of Kings crowd of 23 December 2010 under a PRIME hoodie and interviewed by Angelica Brooks, he opened his PRIME run at ReVolution 238 on 1 February 2011 by beating Tom Walczak, beat Violence Jack, lost to Alexandra Pierce, took the Intense Championship from Lindsay Troy on 21 March 2011, defended it against Jacob McKail in a steel cage at Culture Shock on 31 July 2011, and was billed the final PRIME Intense Champion at his last match, a time-limit draw with Sun Tzu at ReVolution 248 on 18 July 2012. His PRIME card counts 2010 as the first year since 2003 he made no televised appearance anywhere, and names PRIME the one company he had publicly promised never to work for. The show record also has him as a surprise entrant in the Dual Halo at Culture Shock 2008, Night Two, on 15 March 2008, billed by the commentators as the PTC legend and eliminated thirteenth, by Dusk's superkick. In 2011 it adds the ReVolution 243 Battle Royal on 1 April, in which he beat Chainz before Brian Postal pinned him; the opening of ReVolution 244 on 14 April, where he stood in the ring as the new Intense Champion between the Codemaster and Thanatos, and a double countout with Big Bear later that night; an appeal to pray for Japan at ReVolution 246 on 18 May; and, at ReVolution 247 on 16 June, a no contest with Brian Postal and a countout win over his own bodyguard Thanatos that put him in that year's Dual Halo.

tenures.source: Global Championship Wrestling's own backstage database (accession 0159) — its own biography card and its own appearance record: 21 match and 13 segment appearances over 20 of its cards; and the federation's own show pages for WorldWide 23 to 26, FallOut and Devil's Night 2005, donated by GCW's founder (2026-10-06, an e-mail donation)
tenures.note: His whole period in this federation runs from 1 September 2005 to 20 July 2008. Its own record holds 34 appearances over its cards, 9 October 2005 to 20 July 2008, and 25 roleplays of his own. The show pages GCW's founder donated in 2026 add the start of the run: arriving at Annihilation (28 August 2005) to challenge Rich Rollins, he made his GCW ring debut on WorldWide 23 (1 September 2005) with a submission win over Johnny Borealis, beat Octavian, Typhoid Mary and Trey Tremendous on WorldWide 24 to 26, and met Rollins in a no contest at FallOut (circa 25 September 2005, the date the fed's own advance card bills; the page itself prints Thursday, 29 September 2005) and a declared draw at Devil's Night (30 October 2005). Its own biography card for him opens “Seymour Almasy's GCW run is among the most interesting tenures of the Final Fantasy's career. Seemingly on track to the GCW World Title early on, his run was derailed by the arrival of four collagues of his from Global Wrestling. Dubbing themselves Dies Irae, Virgil Ambrosi, Vivica J. Valentine, Lia Ambrosi, and Dawn McFarlane”, and closes the arc “The final straw may have been McFarlane's victory over Seymour in the semi-finals of the Rampage tournament of 2006, the closest Almasy ever got to the GCW World Title, and a defeat suffered at the hands of a woman he loved.” He held its World Tag Team Championship with Virgil Ambrosi, won 21 March 2006 from vacant and lost 7 May 2006, off its own Tag Team Title History page, reign 16. His own Fed Titles field on that card reads “GCW World Tag Team Champion (w/ Eva VanLorne and Virgil Ambrosi)”, three holders against the page's two, and both readings stand. His billed hometown here, “The Imperial Capital of Archades”, is a fifth invented place across the federations he worked, and his finisher here “Hinamizawa Syndrome OR Geostigma” a fourth; every telling stands. The 2005 show pages bill him otherwise than that card: the ring announcer brings him out “from the Royal City of Airyglyph, weighing in at one hundred eighty one pounds” on WorldWide 23, and at 181 pounds again at FallOut and Devil's Night 2005, the weight his UWF roster biography gives; he enters to “'Otherworld' by Nobuo Uematsu” (WorldWide 26), his LOW and PRIME theme, which plays for him on all six of those cards; Devil's Night has “his silver hair and armor flashing in the light” and its commentary credits “his incredible Almasy Synthesis style”. WorldWide 26's commentary (circa 22 September 2005) says he had “proved exactly why he held the PTC Global Championship”, which agrees with PTC's own title history: two reigns of his precede that night, July 2003 to March 2004 and 22 August 2004 to 24 January 2005, and his third came on 27 September 2006.

For the 2005-06 leg: bio 4413, "Emoticon" — its own bio card, ring-entrance script, in-ring code of conduct, 22-match self-kept record and 19 roleplays — with the federation's own show texts for booking 2231 (Evolution, 21 August 2005) and booking 2264 (the November 2005 pay-per-view). Corroborated from outside the federation by the served PTCpedia entry, promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-seymour-almasy-2008.html, whose section "Emoticon in Global Wrestling" names the same two honours. His last appearance in Global is Showdown in Tokyo, 29 November 2005 (booking 2264); the tenure's last_seen of January 2006 is the last word about him, not an appearance: on Reload of 12 January 2006 (booking 2265 ¶128) the owner names him among those who left.
tenures.note: Under his own name he is first seen in a video package on Evolution of 15 December 2003, "the reigning PTC Global Champion" with the words "THE CONTRACT IS SIGNED", and arrives on 19 January 2004. On Global Reload (2 February 2004) he headlined against Ice, who beat him and walked off with his PTC belt, Global's own commentary noting the bout "was not a official PTC Match", so no title changed hands. Global's Overload of 6 February 2004 replays the match, and ends with a PTC official taking the belt back from Ice: "I'll see that this gets back to it's rightful owner." He teamed with El Lunes Mascara as La Ultimo Fantasia to beat the Souls of the Black Lotus, lost to Maverick Reno, and lost a triple threat that Reno won at High Octane on 29 February 2004, his last match under his own name. He returned on 27 May 2005 behind a mask, as Emoticon, "Chivalry's Last Stand" and "the Soul of the Poet", from Marseilles, France. He reached the semi-finals of Master of the Mat VI, took the Global Television Championship from Dawn McFarlane at Evolution on 21 August 2005 with a victory roll, and defended it against Elia Smith eight days later. The same year he won the federation's King of the Death Match, which earned him a shot at the World Championship. At Showdown in Tokyo on 29 November 2005 he unmasked on the way to the ring for that match — "EMOTICON'S ALMASY! I DON'T KNOW HOW, AND I DON'T KNOW WHY, BUT ONE OF THE BIGGEST NAMES IN THE HISTORY OF PRIMETIME CENTRAL'S BEEN IN GLOBAL WRESTLING FOR THE PAST SIX MONTHS!" — walked out "still clad in the black latex of Emoticon", lost to Christian Zenith by disqualification with a chair shot, and thanked the crowd: "THANK YOU, GLOBAL! THANK YOU FOR EVERYTHING!" Crossfire II of 3 July 2005 is narrated from both sides: Global's own write-up has Leinad Soma knock Emoticon off the apron to win the WMW-vs-Global battle royal with the two of them the last men in it, and bio 4413's own match list records the same.

The Emoticon mask identity (already carried as an aka on this record, evidenced from Global Wrestling's own database per the note field below) is confirmed independently by the PTC forum's own "Book of the Courtier" serial, signed "- Emoticon" and referring to the Infinite Gauntlet Championship as its own season's prize — consistent with this record's existing note that Emoticon "took... the PTC Infinite Gauntlet from Rich Rollins." The later 2006 run ("Insanity Prelude" / "The Fall of the House of Almasy") is written under Almasy's own name and stages a first-person crisis — a frightening late-night call, a flight to New York — narrated as events his own "publicist" might dispute, alongside a comic vignette ("Reach Out And Touch Someone") built around a fan's insistence that his PTC Extreme Title opponent Hoyt Williams is literally the son of God.

tenures.role: wrestler — World Heavyweight Champion (2009)
tenures.source: ACW's own write-ups of 15 March to 4 June 2009 in Argyle's 30 September 2026 export (accession 0159; bookings 3354-3364) and the fed's World Heavyweight belt-history page; and, from the fed's 2009 site, its biography card for him (Wayback capture of 15 April 2009, /promotions/acw/archive/seymour-almasy-acw-bio-2009-site.html) and its chatter archive (Wayback capture of 14 April 2009, /promotions/acw/archive/acw-chatter-archive-2009-site.html).
tenures.note: He came back for the fed's one-off show in Montreal on 15 March 2009 and lost its main event to Alias by a spoken "I quit!". He won the vacant World Heavyweight Championship in the tournament final on the Courage of 9 April 2009, beating Andy Sharp. At Legends III on 4 June 2009, the night he was to defend it against Violence Jack in the main event, he was found unconscious in a straight jacket, and Max Danger won the championship in a battle royal. In the weeks after, the fed's shows ran a storyline asking who had attacked him; the write-ups never answer it, and he does not appear on the fed's later 2009-11 shows. The fed's 2009 site carried a new biography card for him (captured 15 April 2009, /promotions/acw/archive/seymour-almasy-acw-bio-2009-site.html). It gives his in-fiction real name as Jason Seymour Wilson, born 12 June 1981, as his GCW card does, and adds his birthplace, Long Island, New York; bills him as "The Final Fantasy, The Protagonist"; and credits his training to Toshiro Mifune's School of Everlasting Excellence (2005), and before that to the in-house training facilities of the UWF and Global Wrestling. It names Laura Winters, "his ex-wife" (Aerith Heartilly, under the name his own roleplays revealed as hers), among his previous managers, and beside RPQ~! and the Dark Ages lists among his previous teams Dies Irae (with Dawn McFarlane, Lia Ambrosi, Vivica J. Valentine and Virgil Ambrosi), the Youngbloods (with Lew Spectre, Kenny Mercury and Jamie Shock) and the Knightmare Brigade ("with many members of the McClancy family"). It gives his reason for coming back as the fed's fan-inclusive concept, and his goal in two words: "Have fun." His first words of the return are on the fed's own chatter page (/promotions/acw/archive/acw-chatter-archive-2009-site.html) on 15 February 2009, the earliest day the page holds: "Seymour Almasy is ready to get this show on the road." On 31 March 2009, after the one-off show, he posted: "This place is still goddamned insane, and I love it."

notes: The single most decorated character in the archive; record held sacred and frozen. His own escalation gag, across the corpus: "Meaner." -> "MEANERER!" -> "the MEANEREREST~!" His own arc: a grief-fueled hiatus after Jamie Shock hospitalized his wife Aerith Heartilly, a return to win the World Title at the Coronation, and a reconciliation with rival Max Queue that formed RPQ ("Because we're IDIOTS~!"). Named once elsewhere, as a contrast rather than an appearance: the UiWF's own 2010 manifesto (promotions/uiwf/archive/2010-manifesto.html) measures the fed's own smallness against how well he'd done since the UWF closed — a reference, not a tenure; no UiWF record is added here. A THIRD INDEPENDENT PRIMARY-SOURCE CREDIT: Lights Out Wrestling (LOW) ran its own dedicated Seymour Almasy bio card, now served at promotions/low/archive/seymour-almasy-bio-card.html, whose own "Handler Information" block reads, verbatim, "Handler Name: Sean Williams" — corroborating, independently of UWF and XUW, that Sean Simon Williams played this character. A FOURTH, from inside the fiction rather than beside it: NFW's own WRESTLESTOCK I of 20 April 2006 promised Seymour Almasy against Kodiak Vic Creed and served no match, only a narrator's aside saying a computer crash had eaten fourteen pages of the write-up — and the aside speaks to him by name, "But alas, Sean Williams fear not, Jesus' sibling is incubating in your hard drive as we speak." Orphan, the Spirit of ACW Champion of 2012, is this character under a later ring name. The fed's own fan board states that Orphan "competed as Seymour Almasy" in an earlier ACW era; the founder ruled the connection high-confidence, so the two records are one character under two ring names. PTC's own encyclopedia, in its 2008 revision, is the only surviving account of the masked persona he wrestled under when he stepped away from his own name — Emoticon, who took Global Wrestling's Television Championship and the PTC Infinite Gauntlet from Rich Rollins before Almasy came back under his own. His last roleplay of his own on PTC's board, "Final Fantasy" (11 August 2008), is written from the crowd and staged as the last match of his career: a woman at the barricade watches him come out to his old entrance music, jumps the guardrail and kisses him in front of sixteen thousand people, and turns out to be the wife whose death the preceding rounds had used against him. It closes on her saying that after four years it is finally good to be herself again.

tenures.bio:
Takayuki Mori, always the odd fellow, entered the Demon Dojo in February of 2003 on a dare that he was unable to get into better shape then had already done. Mori known in his high school as somewhat of a risk taker and gambler and was offered a substansial amount of money by his friends alike to try to get something atheltic and pro wrestling was his first choice.
Mori then was broken in and shown what discipline and determination would take the youngster, eventually even transforming from a some what bulky youngster into a well toned, muscular warrior who has taken pride in his new way of life and even shedding his well known locks to prove that he had gone through a transformation. Mori wished to distinguish himself from the rest of his peers and felt his art of pro wrestling would show his distance from his peers as he chose the road of the throw back wrestling of the Southern territories of the 80's and using more of a balance of power and catch as can style which is a delight to watch as you litterally are seeing a throw back to the vintage 'Wrastlin' of the 80's and how Mori got his nick name in 'Classic'. Mori is only a first year student has proven his worth as he has made his way to the main roster and even earned himself a spot in the ALPHA Cup 2004, Mori then stunned the world when he managed to defeat seasoned veteran Katsuji Shoda to make it to the semi final of the ALPHACup where he showed much spirit before being down by thewinner Craig Williams. Mori feeling his time in Japan was over, ventured over to UWF where he feels he can excel as a pro wrestling and grow personally as a man. Mori shows much potential and great love of pro wrestling, definitley a fire which no one wants to touch.

CANONICAL CHOICE: tessa-windsor (UWF), the richest of the three rows — two title reigns, a roleplay presence and a recorded relationship, against tessa-windsor-xcwf's own two reigns with no appearances and tessa-windsor-low's own single bio-card tenure. Read again for the cross-federation census: the same article is the second independent PTCpedia account joining the three separately-held Chris Storm rows, narrating his PCW tag reign with this character, his move to the DWO, the Rush Pro reunion and the UWF split from her side, and it is cited as such on chris-storm-pcw, chris-storm-pcw and chris-storm-pcw. tenures.note: Billed “The HIT” on the Ikusa IV card of 4 June 2002, in a six-man tag alongside Ali Khadaffi and Carl Kimbell. PURE's own columnist ranks him fifth in the Heavyweight division and second in the Jr. Heavyweight one, names him among the finalists of the PURE Jr. Heavyweight Title tournament alongside Kensuke Suzahara and The End, and calls him an “IWO superstar known for his extreme love of dangerous matches and mathematics.” His run at the belt is dated by the fed's own scripts. At Ikusa, Expo '70 Stadium, Osaka, on 14 April 2002 he beat Cege Hayabusa in a Jr. Heavyweight Title tournament round with the Four Thirds Pi Times Radius Cubed. At Ikusa II, Matsumoto Stadium, Nagano, on 28 April 2002 he reached the three-way the fed billed on air as the crowning of its first ever champion, against Kensuke Suzahara and The End: he had Suzahara in the Word Problem and was closest of the three to winning it when a masked man pulled Suzahara out of the ring, and The End made him tap to Never Again to win it. At Ikusa V, Sapporo Dome, on 16 June 2002 he and Charlie Loc beat The End and Brian Simon with the belt on the line, finishing The End with a double powerbomb into a blue thunder facecrusher and covering him for the three, and the fed's own ring announcer called it: “Winner…and NEW PURE JUNIOR HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION…THE HARDCORE ISOSCELES TRAPEZOID!!!” It is the PURE Jr. Heavyweight Championship his own PCW bio card claims, and the fed's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history numbers him its second champion: “Pinned The End during a six man tag team match to win the title at Ikusa III”, the shape of the Ikusa V bout under another show's name. The fed's own earlier paperwork bills The End because The End held the belt when it was written — the division rankings of 2 May 2002 and the Ikusa IV card of 4 June 2002 both predate the change — and its own champions page carries only the holder of the moment, in states that begin in January 2003. His own PURE roster card is the one document that reads against the reign: its PURE title-history field gives “None as of yet” and its PURE award field is blank. All of it stands. The same card confirms his masked run: its own bio text ends “Masking himself, he is now ready to face the best in PURE”, and PURE v2.0 Ikusa 3 wrestles him masked throughout (the text has Enmity grabbing “the back of his mask” and a cut opening “under the mask”). The card does not mention a win over Ivan Stanislav at PURE, which stands uncorroborated — PURE v2.0 Ikusa 3's own commentary says only that Stanislav is the one man ever to survive the Four Thirds Pi Times Radius Cubed, which is a kickout, not a win. The run reaches further than the Ikusa IV card alone shows: he appears at Gekito 1 on 14 August 2002 (billed for a post-show autograph signing, not on the card) and wrestles Enmity on PURE v2.0 Ikusa 3, a show the record can place no closer than 2002 — so the span closes at year precision. PURE's own news row of 7 January 2003 calls him “the former PURE athlete and now PCW breakout star Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid”, closing the run from the other side. The card's own “real name” field reads “Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid/Horribly Insane Trapezoid,” the phrase on his concept sketch. Three cards disagree gently on vitals: UWF bills him from Ashville, North Carolina at 230 lbs and Heel; PCW and PURE both bill Salt Lake City, Utah (221 lbs PCW, 222 lbs PURE), and PURE bills him Neutral where UWF bills Heel — his alignment shifting between feds and eras. PURE's own setup move, “Parallel Bases,” named without a number, plausibly the seed of UWF's later numbered “Parallel Bases IV.”

tenures.bio:
The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid has had a very interesting life, to say the least. He is a man of many talents, and almost as many quirks. When one lives in Mormon Salt Lake City, and is an atheist, one can expect many oddities.



He was born to loving parents Jeffrey and Maria in a nice middle class neighborhood in Salt Lake City. Soon after his birth, the loving couple had family over at their house, to celebrate the HIT's birth. To this day, his first and last name are unknown. Since he has legally changed his name to The HIT, (Mr. Trapezoid for teaching) and his parents will not speak to the media, it is likely this information will remain forever unknown.



While passing young HIT to an uncle, Jeffrey unfortunately bobbled the child, dropping the infant on the side of his head. Maria immediately called 911, and the paramedics arrived, rushing the baby to the hospital. At first, it appeared no real damage was done. However, in his emergency room, young Trapezoid woke up next to a second grade student, who was desperately studying his shapes. One had been carelessly left on his bed. Trapezoid saw it...and the image on it, an isosceles trapezoid, would change the HIT's life forever.



In his early years, he believed that he WAS an isosceles trapezoid. He enjoyed counting games from the time he was six months old. He was well ahead of everyone else in his classes mathematically, studying such subjects as geometry and algebra when he was in 6th grade. He finished the most advanced calculus course his high school had to offer by 9th grade, leaving the school no choice but to bus him to Brigham Young University to take more advanced mathematics.



Sadly, this would be the best college education he would get. His parents were too poor to send him to college, so he attended a local two-year community college, and graduated with honors, in math of course.



His degree was in business, a subject he despised. However, he knew mathematics was his passion. So, he decided to use his degree to get something he always wanted....



A substitute teaching license.



Going back to Brigham Young High School, The HIT stepped in as a substitute geometry teacher. His odd teaching techniques and bizarre behavior quickly made him a favorite substitute among students. While nearly being barred for life due to his substitute health teaching foray, after persuading the principal with what would come to be known as the SAS Postulate, The HIT was granted a permanent position as a 10th grade Geometry teacher, known to all as Mr. Trapezoid.



Many of his students were wrestling fans, as was The HIT. For years, the HIT had been practicing on the side, joining various schools. He signed a contract with the IWO's IWO Minor League, or the IML. He then worked out a deal with the school, in which he would only teach one period a day to allow for his schedule. This makes each of his students extra special.

He debuted in the IML to rave reviews, capturing the IML United States Title in a three way match against Lance McNally and the champion Phyre with a 450 splash. Soon after though, he got the call up to the IWO. Dropping the belt to The Executioner, he was ready for the next stage of his career.



In the IWO, he came out fast. Many expected him to be an utter joke, yet he rose quickly through the ranks. Facing Jax Stone for the IWO North American title, he dropped one fall to Jax's Drop Like a Stone, yet took two straight falls for the title. He held this for about fifteen days, before dropping it to "The Real Heel" Evan Levine.



From here, he was booked to take on Samuel Potright in a Trick or Treat match, the second of its kind. Trick or Treat II started out as being over the Extreme title, but quickly turned into a rivalry. The HIT emerged victorious in one of the bloodiest matches of all time, but his injury toll was staggering. Over 200 stitches, a broken leg, second degree burns over around 15 percent of his body..all of this forced him to vacate the Extreme Title a day later.



While on the shelf for six months, the HIT's warped mind went even further off the deep end, as he formulated a plan to go after Potright. Competing under a mask as Why, he assaulted Potright, and kidnapped his lovely wife Beth. After using a knife to draw her blood, and then drink it from a glass, he convinced the then World Champion to accept Trick or Treat III for the World Title. 



After the most emotional, violent, and sadistic match in the history of professional wrestling, Sam Potright drove Trapezoid headfirst into the mat in overtime with War Within a Breath to defeat him. However, an executive quirk left The HIT World Champion, and Samuel unable to see Beth for the rest of his life. At this point, The HIT was heartbroken. He had the World Title...but he couldn't live with causing the emotional demise of his nemesis. He excersized a loophole in the match contract...sending him into retirement and surrendering the title, yet earning him Potright's undying respect...for then.



As he recovered from this, even more insane match, he received a call from an unlikely man: Kent Anathason. He needed someone to join himself and Nuke in Primetime Championship Wrestling, to form a group called Neurosis.



Neurosis formed in the summer of 2001, fighting groups such as the Dark Ages. Quickly, things degenerated, as Neurosis was thrown headlong into the path of The Red Army. Anthason and Nuke quickly left, despite HIT and Nuke teaming to nearly overthrow Da Westsidaz reign as tag team champions of PCW. This left the HIT alone to battle The Red Army. Despite much opposition from groups like The European Union, The HIT received no help in his battles.



He eliminated Alexander Popov and Nikita Morozov from PCW, while capturing the PCW Cruiserweight Title from White Mexican, and the Television Title from Kid Wonder. Finally though, his run came to an end. In a retirement match against Rent-A-Hero, Ivan Stanislav, leader of The Red Army, planted HIT with The Red Scare, allowing RAH to pick up a win, and evict HIT from PCW. He immediately swore vengeance on both men.



It didn't take him long to find a new federation, signing on with Epic Wrestling. In a Poisoned Pyramid Deathmatch, he won the promotions North American Title, holding it for two months before dropping it to nemesis Samuel Potright, and leaving.



At this point, The HIT went looking back to PTC for work. He found PURE, a new Japanese promotion starting up. Seeing this as a perfect opportunity to test his skills, the HIT began a makeover.



Masking himself, he is now ready to face the best in PURE. Can the HIT succeed here? We shall see...

mask now covers his face. While his trademark red afro is still visable, a 

dark black mask obscures his features, a giant red 'X' drawn on it. He wears a red cape over his shoulders, and a red and black shirt, with a silver trapezoid on it. His pants are all silver, with black boots.

notes: Sean's other creation alongside Almasy. See /promotions/pcw/ for the PCW footprint. His own signature UWF bout: a THC Title feud with Killer Dude decided in an actual miniature-golf-course deathmatch. Voice, in full: "Because I am gonna beat you down. Right into the grass... I AM GONNA KICK YO ASS!" and "(Fade in) The HIT: I am better than Laguna. (Fade out)." MERGE: hardcore-isosceles-trapezoid-uwf, a thin duplicate stub minted separately under Sean's character's own full ring name rather than the already-registered "H.I.T." aka, has been folded into this record — three show appearances it alone carried (uwf-sas-2003-08-03, uwf-wnu-2003-05-21, and the consolidated uwf-sas-2003-12-14) now point here instead. No new fact beyond what the merged tenure/match rows already show; the stub is deleted, not just aliased, to keep Sean's own record singular. IWO, the Internet Wrestling Organization of iwo-online.com, is a federation his own cards claim and IWO's own news confirms; it is recorded here and not yet minted as a tenure. PCW's own biography card for him (bio 509) lists among his other federations' honours "IWO North American Champion, IWO Extreme Champion, IWO World Heavyweight Champion (technically, reign was annuled at his own request)"; PRIME's own card (bio 21) gives his other federations as "IWO, IML, PURE, UWF, PCW, RPW"; and SCCW's own card (bio 3649) gives them as "IML, IWO, PCW, PURE, PRIME, UWF" and opens his biography on a career begun "in the minor league feeder system of the then dominant Internet Wrestling Organization". Three federations' own databases carry the same claim, down to a reign annulled at his own request. IWO's own news names him twice, in posts it made to CyberSlam's eSlam board that are served on CyberSlam's wing. On 16 May 2000: "Hardcore Isoceles Trapezoid has been furious with the staff backstage and has been promised a World Title match against Psycho Jay within the next month!" (promotions/cyberslam/archive/eslam-120-iwo-michael-dudley-psycho-jay-news.html). On 25 May 2000, its own "IWO ONLINE E-WIRE" press release for the May Mayhem pay-per-view of 28 May 2000: "The past few weeks have seen numerous IWO super stars, including Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid, Psycho Jay, G-Dogg, and others duke it out in an effort to gain a mental advantedge over one another coming into this match." (promotions/cyberslam/archive/eslam-190-iwo-official-mayhem-press-release.html). That puts him on IWO's roster by May 2000, more than a year before his first PCW appearance of August 2001. Sean's own words name the run too: "I was in the OLD ass IWO as Capital Punishment and The HIT" (PTC forum, topic 11465, post 2, 29 November 2004); Capital Punishment is his own record, capital-punishment-acw. IWO is not a wing: it is the frontier row "IWO (H.I.T.'s original fed)" until its own pages are collected, so no IWO tenure and no IWO title reign is written yet. The titles are his cards' claim; IWO's own news confirms that he wrestled there and was promised a World Title match, and does not itself name a reign. The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid enters Round 25 out of retirement, and the roleplay is about noticing he is coming back before he admits it: he stops dyeing his hair brown, stops seeing a barber, and lets the red afro grow back, while his own trainees find that practice matches have stopped being technical contests. He reads his own scars by which match each came from — a Poisoned Pyramid Deathmatch with Sirian in the UWF, a PCW Mall Brawl — and calls the character his coping mechanism, "a zany way to lash back at the world". PRIME's contract forbids him working for another company; he notes that it says nothing about the Gauntlet. He signs up as three letters.
caption: A geometry pun played dead straight as a hardcore wrecking machine, Sean's second UWF creation alongside Almasy, with four reigns with the Hardcore title, one of them won by pinning a table. Before UWF he wrestled in IWO, whose own news of May 2000 had him promised a World Title match. At Epic Wrestling he won the North American Championship on 23 December 2001 in a Poisoned Pyramid Deathmatch of his own devising. In 2005 PRIME saw him purge the Trapezoid to wrestle as Justin Williamson, the Deville's Disciple, and win the Tag Team Championship with Angelo Deville as Manifest Destiny.

name: 'The Savior' Jason Christy

tenures.source: UWF CGI roster database (Wave 8) — mainwebsite_html/roster/, not previously registered
tenures.bio:
Appearance: Jason has a built body with very little body fat. His body is somewhere between Billy Gunn and Lex Luger. Although hailing from England he has a rich tan. When wrestling he wears short black tights, black kneepads, black boots, and black elbow pads. He has sun-bleached hair that comes down to his shoulder blades, always pulled back in a ponytail. He is usually unshaven. On his way to the ring he wears a gown similar to Ric Flairs, but his are black.

Gimmick/Personality: No real gimmick. He is very arrogant, cocky, and aggressive. Likes to insult his opponents. Basically the most typical professional wrestling heel you could imagine.

Background: Jason was always a very competitive person. Born into an equally sports orientated family, he played some form of sport as soon as he could walk. For the physicality and grittiness of it, Jasons favourtie sport when he was younger was rugby union. With his height and frame he excelled in this sport and became very used to pushing his bodys performance to its limits. At the age of
twenty-four the thirst for individual competition turned him to professional wrestling. He also loved the showmanship involved. From then on he has trained and wrestled, and has grown too big for the small ponds of independent
federations. This has brought him to the big leagues.
