name: Tsunami Oni

tenures.hometown: Originally from Masuda, Japan, now residing in San Francisco, CA
tenures.finisher: Onipacalypse — Reverse dragonrana into a back-mounted dragon sleeper. This move is typically reserved for high-profile matches.
tenures.bio:
Tsunami Oni... When he burst on the scene, he was a masked supervillain determined to take over the world with his foul-mouthed dominatrix sidekick, Shiatsu. While he never did take over the world (although he did steal the launch codes to America's nukes when Dubya left them in a White House bathroom, subsequently using one to blow up the Loch Ness Monster), he did manage to capture the TV, Intercontinental, and World titles (the last two he held simultaneously for a brief time before 'losing' the IC belt in a Paper, Rock, Scissors Match against his then-ally, the Prodigy) as well as winning the notorious Contest of Champions. Some career highlights include...

1. Having PeTA activists in bunny suits assault Seymour Almasy

2. Beating Digital Mortality with an aluminum baseball bat while singing 'Take Me Out to the Ballgame.'

3. The Paddle on the Pole match between Shiatsu and the Dominatrix.

4. FAT MURPHY~! and the Table, Ladders, and Cats match.

5. The Evilutionary War and the subsequent ladder match against Unforgiven.

6. Using ShadowBlade's head as a tee after running him over with a golf cart.

7. The formation of the Network of Operatives for the Global Overthrow and Obliteration of Democracy, better know simply as N.O.G.O.O.D.

8. The debut of the Flying Monkey Bomb, greatest triple-team move ever, on Moraless (with the assistance of the Local NVA Company.)

9. Creating an imperfect duplicate of himself known as Bizarro Oni.

Following Live and Loud in 2003 (in which he won the right to be called Greatest Cruiserweight Ever), Oni unmasked and vanished. He recently returned with a new look and slightly changed attitude, but still a success, winning the fifth Regal Rumble at Terror in Tokyo. Now more of an anti-hero that a supervillain, he allied with Unforgiven, Slasher, and Misfit in the drowningPOOL. Although the dP faded, Tsunami Oni's success did not and he has recently won the UWF World championship for a second time.

Strengths - Quite possibly the UWF's greatest high-flyer. Supremely confident and daring. Cunning strategist and master at rule-bending (not to mention rule-breaking). 

Weaknesses - Usually gives up size and strength to his opponents. High-risk moves have resulted in multiple knee surgeries. Past betrayals have made him an untrustworthy ally.
tenures.source: roster/bio/tsunamioni.txt (UWF CGI roster database, W8)

tenures.bio:
White Tiger is the nephew of Uncle Oscar, the original White Tiger. He has trained dilligently and his years of hard work and his unbeatble spirit gotten him... nowhere. Although he can always be counted on to put up a good fight, his win-loss record leaves something to be desired. Then again, maybe losing to World champs like Ruff Ryder and Jamie Shock ain't so bad. 

White Tiger took some time off to concentrate on his film career with Mucha Macho Movies, maker of B-grage action flicks. He has recently returned to the UWF, this time as a member of the Masked Monkeys, Richard Hayes' crack security team. So far, he's managed to get his butt kicked by Jay Vyper and the drowning POOL, but, without question, there will be even more butt-kickings in the future.

tenures.note: Five GIWF cards put him on screen. Global of 24 May 2000: Nephilim brings "Chris Hatchet" into the arena to meet the under-commissioner, and the commentary names him ""Cutthroat" Chris Hatchet, or more commonly known now as RiVeN. That's Celest's little brother". Stable Wars 2000: introduced as "the Professional World Wrestling World Champion, "Cutthroat" Chris Hatchet" and "manager for the evening" of the Order of the Hammer; he puts Ole Gus through a table. Suicide of 11 February 2001: "RiVeN, the brother of Celest and The Preacher" arrives during Celest's handicap match and attacks Benito Cavalera with him. Suicide of 18 February 2001: RiVeN pinned Benito Cavalera. Global of 21 February 2001: he rushes to the scene after Unforgiven's attack on Celest.The GIWF's own broadcasts name two debuts and both are recorded (#sources-disagree): Stable Wars 2000 as "the GIWF debut of Cutthroat Chris Hatchet", and the Mission IMPossible 2001 preview as "Chris Hatchett, or "RiVeN," made his GIWF debut in the handicap match that Thunder wouldn't show up for" (it names no date; his arrival on screen in Celest's handicap match is the Suicide of 11 February 2001, whose commentary says his earlier stay was "oh so brief"). Joined to this record on the evidence recorded in its identity row.

The GIWF's Chris Hatchet of 2000 and 2001 (billed RiVeN and "Cutthroat" Chris Hatchet, Celest's brother) is this record: merged on a presumption, not past the bar. The UWF card of 10 March 2002 bills "The Anarchist" Chris Hatchett at 295 pounds, the weight the GIWF's Suicide of 18 February 2001 bills RiVeN at. The GIWF stages him as the PWW World Champion and, with Shadow, a PWW Tag Team champion; the same UWF card has PWW wrestlers on its roster ("the obviously PWW member, Shadow"). The GIWF and the UWF are one line (iwf, giwf, uwf), and Celest wrestled for both. No page names the GIWF's RiVeN and the UWF's Anarchist together.
